claims.text: The initial material is as-cast HfMoTaTiZr.
Replacing heavy elements such as Hf and Mo with lighter refractory elements such as Nb and Ti will reduce the alloy density.
The proposed substitution can preserve strong room-temperature mechanical performance.
The proposed substitution can preserve strong high-temperature mechanical performance.
Changes in alloy composition and microstructure mediate the effects of the substitution.
Optimization of composition and microstructure may maintain or improve mechanical properties after substitution.
The substituted alloy is predicted to have approximately 5–10% lower density than the as-cast baseline.
The substituted alloy is predicted to avoid a significant loss of yield strength at room temperature.
The substituted alloy is predicted to avoid a significant loss of yield strength at 1000 °C.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a density of 10.21 g cm−3.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a room-temperature yield strength of about 1600 MPa.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has an elevated-temperature yield strength of about 855 MPa.
The proposed testing boundary extends from room temperature to 1600 °C under loading up to yield.
The controlled experiment will systematically replace heavy elements with lighter refractory elements and compare density, yield strength, and microstructure.
The hypothesis is rejected if density decreases by less than 5% relative to the baseline.
The hypothesis is rejected if yield strength decreases by more than 10% at either room temperature or 1000 °C relative to the baseline.
